searchText: <@!543900561460822016> Probably worth putting a rationale for "Why does the envelope have a nonce?" in 2733. I figured it out, but it took me a bit and I looked in Rationale for an answer first. Also, why RLP? I think the consensus is that RLP isn't great for transactions. Just to avoid being the EIP that introduces SSZ formally into ETH 1? The child transaction says: > The type field is used to denote whether the Child signer wishes to delegate the max_gas_price and gas_limit choice to the TransactionPackage signer. yet the TransactionPackage doesn't have a spot to put the gas limit. Step 6 of Execution says to prepare result, but it doesn't specify if that result will be available the first frame of the next `ChildPackage` if it is the last transaction in a `ChildPackage` or not. The discussion in 2711 has arguments for why gas limit, gas price, one, or both should be decided by the sponsor vs the signer. In 2733 you only have 2 options, all by sponsor or all by signer. Recommend adding a rationale on why you do not provide an option for sponsor setting one and signer setting the other. Consider defining two `ChildTransaction` types, one that has a `gas_limit` and one that does not. > Probably worth putting a rationale for "Why does the envelope have a nonce?" in 2733. <@!301186049323958275> yes good point, will do > Also, why RLP? I think the consensus is that RLP isn't great for transactions. Just to avoid being the EIP that introduces SSZ formally into ETH 1? Mainly the latter, if there is very strong consensus i'm not against adding. > yet the TransactionPackage doesn't have a spot to put the gas limit. yes, if the type is `0x01` then the package signer can choose *whatever* limit they wish for each `ChildTransaction`, because the child signer didn't sign over the limit > Step 6 of Execution says to prepare result, but it doesn't specify if that result will be available the first frame of the next ChildPackage if it is the last transaction in a ChildPackage or not. do you think it's confusing as is? step 4 says "f there are no more child transactions, goto 8" -- thus bypassing the result computation and therefore no result would be present for the first tx in the next package > Recommend adding a rationale on why you do not provide an option for sponsor setting one and signer setting the other. will do > Consider defining two ChildTransaction types, one that has a gas_limit and one that does not. Do you think that the `type` field does not offer the same functionality? Ah, I missed the skip in step 4. Re: type field It does, but it references an object that is never defined IIRC. <@543900561460822016> I don't have the EIP open at the moment (and on mobile) but IIRC one of them has an array of "child transactions without gas limit". The type of that should be explicitly defined somewhere. For example, should the gas limit need to be set to zero, or omitted? Rather than just having a variable that says "type is `X - Y` in the variable name. it would be omitted completely, i can define more explicitly Note: this suggestion is a non-normative change, just a clarity improvement. Re: "package signer can choose whatever limit they wish", I get the idea here, there is just nowhere to put that value in the defined type. 🙂 ```go struct TransactionPackage { chain_id: u256, children: [ChildPackage], nonce: u64, gas_price: u256, v: u256, r: u256, s: u256 } ``` No spot for limit here. the limit would be defined per child tx Oh, I'm against that weakly because it makes signing more complicated since the signature isn't over the whole transaction. If you go this route, I think the limit should be *after* the signature. On that general note, I recommend putting the whole signed data into an array. I did this in https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2972 The idea being that you don't have to pluck pieces out of the transaction and then re-encode it in order to validate the signature (QoL improvement). My perspective is that these "signature structures" are being defined on the fly anyways: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/66c3eb2f1a5c6bb4b5a678ce819f9984ac09e246/core/types/transaction_signing.go#L155-L165 I don't have that strong of an opinion though, mostly just erring on the side of simplicity atm Same, but simplicity for all of the tools that sign and validate transactions. Having written a signer, I can say that having to encode twice is annoying and error prone. i appreciate the perspective

excerpts.content:
The child transaction says:
> The type field is used to denote whether the Child signer wishes to delegate the max_gas_price and gas_limit choice to the TransactionPackage signer.
yet the TransactionPackage doesn't have a spot to put the gas limit.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Step 6 of Execution says to prepare result, but it doesn't specify if that result will be available the first frame of the next `ChildPackage` if it is the last transaction in a `ChildPackage` or not.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: The discussion in 2711 has arguments for why gas limit, gas price, one, or both should be decided by the sponsor vs the signer.  In 2733 you only have 2 options, all by sponsor or all by signer.  Recommend adding a rationale on why you do not provide an option for sponsor setting one and signer setting the other.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Consider defining two `ChildTransaction` types, one that has a `gas_limit` and one that does not.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content:

<@!301186049323958275>  yes good point, will do

> Also, why RLP?  I think the consensus is that RLP isn't great for transactions.  Just to avoid being the EIP that introduces SSZ formally into ETH 1?
Mainly the latter, if there is very strong consensus i'm not against adding.

> yet the TransactionPackage doesn't have a spot to put the gas limit.
yes, if the type is `0x01` then the package signer can choose *whatever* limit they wish for each `ChildTransaction`, because the child signer didn't sign over the limit

> Step 6 of Execution says to prepare result, but it doesn't specify if that result will be available the first frame of the next ChildPackage if it is the last transaction in a ChildPackage or not.
do you think it's confusing as is? step 4 says "f there are no more child transactions, goto 8" -- thus bypassing the result computation and therefore no result would be present for the first tx in the next package

> Recommend adding a rationale on why you do not provide an option for sponsor setting one and signer setting the other.
will do

> Consider defining two ChildTransaction types, one that has a gas_limit and one that does not.
Do you think that the `type` field does not offer the same functionality?
